name_en: Okaisan — rice simmered in roasted tea, a stand-in for scarce rice
summary_ja: 番茶を煮出した湯で米を炊く、和歌山で「茶がゆ」を親しみを込めて呼ぶ朝の一杯。山がちで米が乏しかった土地で少ない米を腹持ちよくする知恵とされ、さつまいもや梅干し、金山寺味噌をのせるなど食べ方は家庭ごとに違うという。
summary_en: Rice is simmered in water steeped with roasted tea — what Wakayama fondly calls chagayu. Said to have stretched scarce rice into a filling meal in a mountainous prefecture, it's topped differently by every household, with sweet potato, umeboshi, or kinzanji miso.
source_title: おかいさん／茶がゆ 和歌山県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kakimade Gohan — rice mixed with fish-stock vegetables, no vinegar
summary_ja: 焼き魚の骨でとった出汁で季節の野菜を炊き、酒を加えて炊いたご飯に混ぜ込む。酢は使わずちらし寿司とは一線を画す、日高地方の祝い事や法事に振る舞われてきた混ぜご飯だという。
summary_en: Vegetables are simmered in a stock made from grilled fish bones, then folded into rice cooked with a splash of sake — no vinegar, unlike chirashi sushi. It's a mixed rice dish served at celebrations and memorial gatherings across the Hidaka region.
source_title: かきまでご飯 和歌山県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kaki Maburi — a chirashi-style rice dish made in bulk for guests
summary_ja: 高野豆腐や干ししいたけなど乾物と季節の野菜をすし飯に混ぜ込むちらしずし。「かき混ぜ」がなまった那賀地方の方言「まぶり」が名の由来で、来客が何人来るか分からない祝い事の日にたくさんつくって振る舞われてきた。
summary_en: Dried tofu, shiitake, and seasonal vegetables are folded into sushi rice for this chirashi-style dish. Its name comes from "maburi," a Naga-area dialect word for "mix," and it's made in bulk for celebrations where the number of guests can't be known in advance.
source_title: かきまぶり 和歌山県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Uzumi — rice buried under a clear tofu broth for a memorial meal
summary_ja: しいたけと昆布の出汁に豆腐やしいたけを浮かせたすまし汁の下にご飯を埋め、ゆずやしょうがなど薬味を添える。古座川最奥の平井集落だけに伝わる法事の前夜料理で、京の懐石料理が伝わったとの言い伝えもあるという。
summary_en: Rice is buried beneath a clear broth of shiitake and kelp, floated with tofu and mushrooms, and finished with citrus zest and ginger. Passed down only in the Hirai hamlet deep in the Kozagawa valley for the eve of a memorial service, one account traces it back to Kyoto kaiseki cuisine.
source_title: うずみ 和歌山県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Mame Gohan — spring peas cooked into rice at the peak of harvest
summary_ja: 米が乏しくなる春先に、収穫期を迎えるうすいえんどうをたっぷり炊き込んでかさ増しした、和歌山県中部地域の豆産地に伝わるご飯。塩だけで味付けし、豆の風味と甘みを生かした素朴な一品だという。
summary_en: As rice grew scarce each spring, plump usui peas at the peak of their harvest were cooked into rice to stretch it further, a dish from the pea-growing districts of central Wakayama. Seasoned with nothing but salt, it lets the peas' sweetness and flavor carry the dish.
source_title: 豆ごはん 和歌山県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Shouga Meshi — new ginger cooked straight into the rice pot
summary_ja: 紀の川沿いの砂地で栽培される辛味の少ない新しょうがを、米と一緒に炊き込む和歌山市の一品。爽やかな香りが食欲をそそり、夏場でもさっぱりと食べやすいことから風邪予防や冷え性対策としても使われてきたという。
summary_en: Mild new ginger, grown in the sandy soil along the Kinokawa river, is cooked straight into the rice pot in this Wakayama City dish. Its bright scent whets the appetite and goes down easily even in summer, and it's also been used as a folk remedy for colds and poor circulation.
source_title: しょうが飯 和歌山県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
